evidence.detail: times_from_timezone_code() filters pytz.common_timezones by datetime.now(tz).strftime('%Z') == q.upper(); in summer New York is 'EDT' not 'EST', so only permanently-EST zones (like America/Jamaica) match
time(q) routes to times_from_timezone_code when len(q)<=4, so 'EST' always takes the abbreviation path
No commit in history addresses the EST/Jamaica disambiguation

triage.fix_sketch: In magic/fetcher.py, add a dict CANONICAL_TZ_ALIASES mapping common US abbreviations to their year-round canonical timezone (e.g. {'EST': 'America/New_York', 'EDT': 'America/New_York', 'CST': 'America/Chicago', ...}). In times_from_timezone_code(), check if q.upper() is in CANONICAL_TZ_ALIASES and always include that zone in results (alongside any other current matches). Only magic/fetcher.py needs to change; no schema or data impact.
triage.notes: The static alias map approach preserves existing behavior for legitimate multi-zone abbreviations while always surfacing the expected canonical US zone for common abbreviations.
